Hi Laura — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Aditya (security) and Neha (legal) to own the questionnaire and provide the formal documentation. Answers inline below and next attachment details: 

Answers to your questions:
- Analytics/PII: Redwood does not sell or otherwise share customer PII with analytics vendors. We may use third-party telemetry/observability tools (e.g., Datadog) that receive anonymized/aggregated metrics. Access to customer content is restricted to a very small set of SREs under strict access controls and audit logging.
- Transcript retention: Retention is configurable by the customer. Default retention is 90 days for full conversation transcripts; customers can configure shorter or longer retention periods subject to contract. We persist minimal metadata for routing and billing beyond that window unless customers opt into longer retention.
- Processor role: Redwood acts as a processor under our standard agreement. Subprocessors are engaged as subprocessors (our agreements include flow-down obligations). We don’t consider any subprocessor a co-processor in the typical sense.

What we attached in this message:
- redwood_subprocessors_2026-06.pdf (canonical export: cloud providers, managed services, observability, analytics, identity/KMS providers)
- SOC2-cert-2025.pdf (SOC 2 Type II — most recent audit summary)

High-level subprocessor highlights (from the attached PDF):
- Cloud compute/storage: AWS (us-west-2), GCP (us-central1)
- Object storage: AWS S3 (encrypted at rest), GCS buckets for ephemeral workloads
- Observability: Datadog (metrics/traces, redacted/aggregated traces only)
- Secrets/Keys: AWS KMS / customer-managed keys available for Private deployments
- ML infra partners: Triton deployment partners / model hosting partners (described in subprocessor doc)
